request.spec:
A steward can set a claim's due-by directly (a date entry and a button on a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING
claim; CLAIM_DUE_BY_SET naming the claim and ending old=<old due-by> new=<new>; anyone else or any
other status is refused). A due-by set this way stays as set: a holiday added later does not move
it. Overdue, the late charge, grace and the period the claim belongs to follow the set date.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can set a claim's due-by directly (a date entry and a button on a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING
claim; CLAIM_DUE_BY_SET naming the claim and ending old=<old due-by> new=<new>; anyone else or any
other status is refused). A due-by set this way stays as set: a holiday added later does not move
it. Overdue, the late charge, grace and the period the claim belongs to follow the set date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
`bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` succeed. One is the new "due by override" test; the other three are longer scenario tests in the same spec file, and they still pass.

A steward can now set a claim's due-by directly:
- **On screen:** each claim row has a new date field and a "Set due-by" button. A refusal shows in the row's existing error element.
- **Who and when:** only a steward, and only on a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim. Anyone else, any other status, or a missing date is refused and nothing is written.
- **Audit:** a successful change writes `CLAIM_DUE_BY_SET` naming the claim, ending `old=<old> new=<new>`.
- **Holidays:** a new `due_by_set` flag on claims (migration `V123__claim_due_by_set.sql`) marks a hand-set due-by, and adding a holiday no longer moves those. Copying a claim or cloning a sheet keeps the flag.
- **Figures:** overdue, the late charge, grace and the period already work from the stored due-by, so they follow the set date without further changes.

One addition the request didn't ask for: setting the due-by is also refused when either the old or the new date falls in a closed period, to match how other claim actions behave.
